title: SPARC Cat Surgery Day 0
author: Brett Hanzlicek
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfy9jpz6
materials: Replace the bladder in its orthotopic postion.

steps.title: Prepare Cat for Surgery
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the cat, shave the abdomen, and attach to monitors.

steps.title: Sterilize Surgical Site
steps.instruction: Drape the cat and perform a betadine scrub on the abdomen and genitals.

steps.title: Insert Bladder Catheter
steps.instruction: Insert a 3.5Fr catheter into the bladder through the urethra using surgilube.

substeps.instruction: Retract the foreskin and advance the catheter directly into the center of the triangular shaped glans.
Advance the catheter until resistance is met, then pull back 2-3 cm.

steps.title: Mark and Incise Abdomen
steps.instruction: Prepare the abdominal incision site based on imaging results to locate the bladder.

substeps.instruction: Mark a midline 3-4 cm line with a skin marker.
Make the skin incision with a #15 blade.
Cut through the fat and bluntly dissect the skin off the muscle.
Use a Weitlaner retractor to keep the incision open.

steps.title: Enter Abdominal Cavity
steps.instruction: Access the abdominal cavity to visualize the bladder.

substeps.instruction: Make a small incision in the midline muscle using a scalpel or scissors, ensuring not to go through the other side.
Use a right angle or small hemostat to enter the abdomen bluntly and open the muscle/fascia to the length of the incision.
Spread the abdomen open using the retractor (incorporating musculature) or two fingers.

steps.title: Deliver Bladder
steps.instruction: Extract the bladder from the abdominal cavity.

substeps.instruction: Optionally remove some fluid from the bladder first to decrease the required incision length.
Grasp the bladder with a blunt pick-up and deliver it out of the incision.
Place the bladder on several wet pieces of gauze to avoid contact with fur or instruments.

steps.title: Prepare Bladder for Cystotomy
steps.instruction: Mark and secure the bladder dome for incision.

substeps.instruction: Identify an area on the dome that is less vascular and not covered in fat (avoiding the dorsal ureters near the bladder neck).
Mark a 1 cm line on the dome of the distended bladder using a skin marker.
Place a 4-0 vicryl full thickness stay-suture at each apex of the planned incision and keep them untied in a hemostat.

steps.title: Perform Cystotomy
steps.instruction: Incise the bladder to allow device placement.

substeps.instruction: Incise the bladder using a #10 blade.
Immediately place a closed hemostat or pickup inside the lumen to maintain the opening.
Use tissue scissors to open the rest of the mucosa (the full 1 cm may not be necessary due to bladder stretchability).
Hold one apical suture while an assistant holds the other to prepare for device placement.

steps.title: Close Cystotomy
steps.instruction: Irrigate and seal the bladder incision.

substeps.instruction: Irrigate the bladder with saline.
Close the mucosa with a running 4-0 vicryl suture.
Close the muscle with several interrupted 4-0 vicryl sutures.
Tie the initial stay sutures.
Control any detrusor bleeding with manual pressure or a suture.

steps.title: Perform Leak Test
steps.instruction: Perform a quick leak test while visualizing the bladder incision to determine filling capacity for post-op cystogram and cystometry.

steps.title: Close Abdominal Wall
steps.instruction: Close the abdominal cavity and irrigate the wound.

substeps.instruction: Close the abdominal wall in one layer with 3-0 surgipro running suture.
Optionally place 1-2 interrupted sutures in the middle for extra support.
Irrigate the wound.

steps.title: Close Subcutaneous Layer
steps.instruction: Use leftover vicryl to perform Scarpa's or subcutaneous fat stitches.

steps.title: Close Skin
steps.instruction: Close the skin with simple, interrupted nylon sutures.

substeps.instruction: Place sutures closely together.
Avoid over-tightening the nylon sutures.
Cut the tails short to prevent irritation or interference by the cat.
